att_and_ck_version_comparison.analysis: In v19.2, MITRE ATT&CK introduced the Stealth and Defense Impairment tactics, restructuring Defense Evasion. Because CAM-LDS was authored using traditional Defense Evasion tactics, evaluating against v19.2 increases discrepancies from 8 to 22. v16.1 represents the faithful historical baseline for CAM-LDS ground-truth tactics.

known_limitations: Small Dataset Size: CAM-LDS comprises only 4 attack scenarios (E1..E4) yielding 190 total events and 67 collapsed transition samples at full technique granularity.
Single Run per Archive: Each raw archive represents exactly one execution of an attack campaign; no repeated runs exist to assess within-scenario variance.

Attack Window UTC Assumption: UTC alignment is verified via syslog/auth.log for scenario_1 and scenario_4; for scenario_2 and scenario_3, system timestamps are consistent (Etc/UTC) but lack external time anchors.

Absence of Real C3 Telemetry: The 8 proposal C3 fields (ioc, ioc_type, incident_stage, asset_criticality, cti_confidence, freshness, c3_threat_score, investigation_priority) are null across all 190 events in CAM-LDS. Only local_occurrence is populated (derived by C4 for labeled events).

ATT&CK Tactic Discrepancies: 8 steps in CAM-LDS exhibit discrepancies between AttackMate recorded tactics and official MITRE ATT&CK v16.1 enterprise mappings (e.g. E2-S024 maps T1003.008 to Discovery instead of Credential Access, and E4-S007 maps T1078.003 to Lateral Movement instead of Defense Evasion / Initial Access / Persistence / Privilege Escalation).

Vocabulary Divergence & Coverage Bounds: Cross-episode technique overlap is limited; pooled leave-one-episode-out reachable target coverage is bounded at 52.2% (35/67) for full technique IDs and 58.2% (39/67) for parent IDs.
